audit_notes: Model: Couette flow across the viscous sublayer (thickness delta = 5 nu/u_tau = 5*1.05e-6/0.19 = 27.6 um; 26 um used, consistent) with fixed edge velocity 5 u_tau = 0.95 m/s and a Navier slip wall u(0) = (b/delta) du/dy(0). Analytical: u(y) = U_e (y + b/delta)/(1 + b/delta), wall shear tau = mu U_e /(delta + b). Baseline: same flow with b = 0 (clean silicone foul-release coating has no measurable slip in water). Wall-shear reduction = b/(delta+b) = 5e-8/2.605e-5 = 0.19%. Dimensionless: b+ = b u_tau/nu = 5e-8*0.19/1.05e-6 = 0.009; delta+ = 4.7; Re_tau of the hull boundary layer (delta_BL ~ 1.5 m at 100 m) ~ 2.7e5. This laminar-sublayer model is a lower-bound-type proxy; in real turbulent flow, streamwise slip also weakens near-wall streaks, but for b+ < 0.1 the effect remains below ~1% (Min & Kim 2004), so the order of magnitude is right. Brush slip lengths in the literature are debated: many careful measurements on hydrated brushes find b <= 10 nm or even negative (hydrodynamic thickness adds effective no-slip), so 50 nm is optimistic. Structural/durability check: wall shear of ~18 Pa on a 100 nm brush is harmless mechanically, but abrasion (fenders, cleaning brushes, sand-laden water), hydrolysis of ester/amide linkers in pH 8.1 seawater and oxidative degradation limit such brushes to months, not years; the texture shield idea is not part of this model. Parameters are physically plausible; audit passed with these caveats.

performance_gain.label: Wall shear reduction vs clean foul-release coating

hard_constraints: slip_length <= brush_thickness (apparent slip cannot exceed the hydrated layer scale for a brush)

baseline_description: Clean standard silicone foul-release coating (no-slip wall)
